Anna K: Heads-up — ran a 1h long-context soak (sessions ~100k tokens) against the int8 runtime with bf16 fallback. Observed steady KV-slot growth on prod-sim: +6MB/min/worker; eventually the evicter kicked in and we saw 10–15ms tail spikes.
Alex G: can you paste the profiler counters? GPU vs host?
Anna K: quick numbers from the run: GPU reserved 7.2GB -> 11.1GB, kv_slots allocated 42k -> 78k over 58 minutes, evict_count/sec was ~0.2 until 45m then jumped to ~3.5.
Priya S: leaking slots or fragmentation? did compact/reclaim help?
Anna K: compact on-demand doesn't reclaim enough. Slab map shows many small free spans. Example snippet from slabmap dump:
```
slab:slot_size=128 used=23090 free=12784 small_free_pct=34.8
slab:slot_size=512 used=18440 free=930 frag_est=28.1
total_slots=78022 reserved_pages=1224
```
Marco V: interesting — quantized pages are aligned differently. int8 page layout here is 16KB vs bf16 8KB so internal fragmentation might be higher for mixed-size KV entries.
Sasha L: also check kernel selection logs. For long sequences the runtime chose `matmul_int8_fused` + `prefetch_v2` path which keeps extra prefetch windows open — that could increase residency.
Anna K: confirmed — kernel_table shows `prefetch_window=6` for int8 fused path, bf16 path uses window=3. Prefetch window seems correlated with slot residency.
Alex G: any batching heuristic changes? larger batch sizes can cause more eager prefetch and singleflight contention that prevents reuse.
Anna K: our longctx harness did pick batch_size=32 at 1s latency target. I tried flipping singleflight on prefetch (it was off) — reuse improved noticeably, growth rate halved.
Priya S: did int8 affect end-to-end quality? we need to weigh memory wins vs accuracy.
Anna K: eval on our long-context prompt-suite: int8-only -> lm loss +0.9% relative, top-1 token match -0.7% for sequences >8k tokens. bf16 fallback reduced loss gap to +0.2%.
Marco V: actionable mitigations: 1) reduce prefetch_window for int8 fused kernel 2) enable singleflight coalescing for prefetch 3) compact-on-idle (aggressive compaction when resident growth detected) 4) consider hybrid page sizes or per-layer precision (bf16 for early layers).
Alex G: also try lowering batch target and enabling batch-shrink for long sequences to avoid too-large eager prefetch. Can we gate prefetch by reuse-score?
Sasha L: we could compute a per-key reuse_score from telemetry and skip prefetch for low-score keys. cheap heuristic: if key_hit_rate < 0.03 in last 10k requests -> skip prefetch.
Anna K: I'll run two experiments in canary: A) prefetch_window=3 + singleflight_on B) keep current window but force bf16 for first 6 layers + compact-on-idle. Measure memory growth slope and eval quality.
Priya S: please capture token-level deltas and per-layer attribution for accuracy; we need an explicit rollback threshold (e.g., >1% loss or >1.5% top-1 drop).
Marco V: note also that compact-on-evict is expensive; prefer compact-on-idle or background compaction with rate limit. Could use periodic compaction windows when throughput < X.
Anna K: noted. I'll post perf dashboards after runs.
deploy-bot: Canary planned — schedule request created for 2026-03-22 02:00 UTC (canary/kv-quant-reuse).
Alex G: thanks — if A shows memory slope <1MB/min and loss <0.5% we can roll.
Anna K: will update with numbers. :eyes:
